Subject: CS -> ENG: Context & capacity alignment for PilotAI integration

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. PilotAI is excited to move to Redwood for inference. To get engineering aligned before the formal kickoff, I wanted to share a quick snapshot of our estimated workload and ask for an initial model/context recommendation.

Quick context:
- Product: in-app code-assist + short chat (multi-turn) for devs.
- Expected initial traffic: ~50k MAU (we expect 2.5k DAU average in month one).
- Typical session: 3–5 turns. Average request token size: ~600 tokens. P95 request size: ~2,100 tokens.
- Peak concurrency expectation: spikes during morning US hours, up to ~350 concurrent active sessions.
- Hard constraints: 350ms p95 response target for simple prompts; 1s p95 acceptable for longer code completions.

I've attached a small sample of anonymized request payloads (pilotai_token_samples.csv). Can you and your engineering team propose a shortlist of model variants we should try, recommended context length (4k / 8k / 32k), and a ballpark monthly token estimate for the initial month? Also flag whether this workload looks like a Hosted API fit or we should recommend Dedicated immediately.

Appreciate a quick turn — we're aiming to finalize the mutual action plan (MAP) by next Wednesday.

Best,
Samantha Liu
Head of Product Operations, PilotAI
Samantha Liu | PilotAI

Hi Samantha — thank you for the detailed samples, this is very helpful. Looping in Ben (capacity modeling), Rishi (serving/runtime), and Priyom (implementation CS lead) so we can get an engineering-first read and an initial estimate.

Preliminary read (high level):
- Model shortlist to test (first pass):
  1) redwood-1-medium (8k) — good latency/cost balance for <1k token responses; useful as a fallback.
  2) redwood-1-large (16k) — strong quality for multi-turn code/context; recommended primary candidate.
  3) open-llama-7b-q4_8k — lower cost candidate for high throughput; may need quality checks on code completions.

- Context length recommendation: 16k (start there). Sample tokens show multi-turn context with code + state; P95 at 2.1k per request but combined context for multi-turn and system prompts pushes effective seq length higher. 16k gives room for history + long completions and simplifies rolling forward without immediate retrains.

- Ballpark token estimate (back-of-envelope):
  *DAU and sessions*: 2.5k DAU, assume average 4 requests/day per DAU => 10k requests/day.
  *Avg user request size*: 600 request tokens + 600 response tokens (conservative) = ~1.2k tokens per request.
  *Daily tokens*: 10k * 1.2k = 12M tokens/day.
  *Monthly (30d)*: ~360M tokens/month.

Notes: this is conservative — if response tokens are larger (long code completions) the numbers rise. If you enable prefix/KV caching for repeated system prompts and context snippets, we can reduce served tokens per request.

Recommendation for initial deployment: start with Hosted API for the first 4–6 weeks to validate quality and steady-state token profile. If steady p95 latency or throughput becomes constrained and traffic is close to our Dedicated breakpoints (~250–500M tokens/mo with high concurrency), we should discuss a Reserved (Dedicated) plan.

Next actions:
- Ben: can you run a quick throughput/lantency simulation for redwood-1-large and open-llama-7b-q4 at 16k context? Target: p95 observed latencies and GPU concurrency requirements.
- Rishi: flag any runtime optimizations (quantization, batching profile, prefix cache) we should enable for PilotAI workloads.
- Priyom: prepare a one-page MAP draft with milestones (trial period, canary rollout, quality gates, SLA checkpoint).

I'll pull this into a short MAP doc and share a meeting invite for a technical kickoff next week.

Thanks — Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen

Quick thoughts:
- Quantization: try q4_0 for open-llama candidate to save memory; run quality check on a representative set of code completions (Priyom, can you surface 20 critical test prompts?).
- Batching: 350 concurrent sessions likely to benefit from micro-batching combined with latency-aware routing. We'll surface batching profiles from Ben's runs.
- Caching: we should enable prefix/KV caching for repeated system prompts and common scaffolding snippets — that could reduce served tokens by ~10–20% based on similar customers.
- Fallbacks: plan primary=redwood-1-large (16k), fallback=open-llama-7b-q4 (8k) for cost-based graceful degradation. Ensure prompt engineering avoids brittle context reliance.

I'll add a short runtime checklist for the MAP doc and include recommended flags for the initial canary.

—Rishi

- Conservative monthly token estimate: ~360M tokens/mo based on submitted samples.
- Recommended starting context: 16k to support multi-turn + code completions.
- Hosted API is fine for a 4–6 week validation; if we see sustained >250M token/mo with high concurrency we should evaluate Dedicated.

Proposed immediate actions (MAP draft):
1) Engineering perf run (Ben) — perf matrix and GPU estimate (deliverable: perf_report_v1) — due: 2025-06-17 EOD.
2) Quality checks (PilotAI & Red) — 20 representative prompts run against shortlist; collect pass/fail and sample diffs — due: 2025-06-19.
3) Canary plan + flags (Rishi) — batching/prefix-cache/quantization settings — due: 2025-06-19.
4) Business/contract touch (Procurement) — review MAP and trial terms, DocuSign to follow — due: 2025-06-23.

I attached a MAP template (MAP_Template.pdf) and an initial estimate workbook. I'll send a calendar invite for a technical kickoff tomorrow at 10:30am PT — please confirm availability.
